text.p: Malaysia's Transwater Corp Bhd revealed profit forecasts for two financial years in reply to a query from the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The firm, in the midst of a major restructuring, said late on Tuesday that net profit for the year to February 26, 1998, will be 11.293 million ringgit and jump to 71.067 million for 1999.
The forecast was based on its acquisition of four companies and a piece of land, which will transform the small engineering company into a property/resort and sewerage treatment concern.
Profit before tax was forecast at 14.341 million ringgit in 1998 and at 71.067 million in 1999, the statement said.
The firm had previously forecast that before the acquisitions, its 1998 net profit would be 3.746 million ringgit.
Transwater has proposed to buy stakes in Tioman Island Resort Bhd, Kota Raya Development Sdn Bhd, Resort Cruises Sdn Bhd, Prime Utilities Bhd and a 1,568-hectare piece of land.
The restructuring led by businessman Wan Adli Wan Ibrahim will see Transwater holding a 19 percent stake in Prime, whose unit has the national sewerage treatment concession.
Tioman Island is a resort operator while Kota Raya operates a shopping complex. Resort Cruises is a shell company which will injected with various assets as part of the restructuring.
